Marksville Historic District, Louisiana
Z28scrambler

Source & image record ↗ · CC BY-SA 4.0

This modern streetscape gives geographic context for John R. Swanton’s Ofo language fieldwork near Marksville, which he described in 1909. The Atlas resized the original photograph and shares this copy under the same license.

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Language records, migrations and descendant-community connections. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] repository.si.edu [2] asjp.clld.org [3] Tunica-Biloxi Tribe of Louisiana

03

A descendant-community connection

The Tunica-Biloxi Tribe identifies Ofo among its ancestral constituents. This gives readers a specific descendant connection in Louisiana while keeping the historical peoples and the present shared government distinct.

Read the sources [3] Tunica-Biloxi Tribe of Louisiana

Our Culture ↗

The Tribe names Ofo among its ancestral constituent peoples and describes its Louisiana location. This supports a specific descendant-community connection through a shared government, without treating Ofo, Tunica and Biloxi as interchangeable identities.

Inspection: Supporting or limited review; see scope

Scope: Complete short culture page read, especially succession, constituent-peoples and Marksville-area reservation paragraphs.

Review recorded: October 21, 2026
